To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the binding of nucleoside derivatives to dextran does not interfere with the complex formation of the substrate with adenosine deaaminase and does not alter the catalytic activity.

the Km and Ki of dextran-bound substrates and inhibitors are higher than that of the corresponding free compounds, that the Vmax of dextran-linked compounds is the same as that of the free compounds, and that the activation energies of dextran-modified substrates and inhibitors do not differ from that of the corresponding compounds in solution.
the dextran-linked nucleosides are good substrates and inhibitors, but not diffusion-controlled.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new class of adenosine analogues which are covalently linked to a polysaccharide support, dextran T70, T80, or T100.
the preparation and properties of dextran-linked nucleosides and their acetal derivatives.
the development of dextran-bound substrates and inhibitors which are suitable for the study of enzyme kinetics and for affinity chromatography of adenosine-deaminase.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the dextran-bound acetals are good substrates for adenosine-deaminase but that they do not fit as well to the enzyme as does the free nucleoside.

the binding of the acetal esters of adenosine to the polymer support leads to a decrease of the catalytic efficiency, but does not interfere with the formation of a productive complex between the enzyme and substrate.
the dextran-bound acetals of adenosine and inosine are not suitable substrates or inhibitors for adenoside deaminase.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the dextran-linked nucleosides are excellent inhibitors of adenosines deaminase and that their use for the preparation of adenosine analogs is limited by the low solubility of the dextran-bound derivatives.
the dextran-linked nucleosides are excellent substrates and inhibitors and that they do not interfere with the catalytic mechanism of adenosine-deaminase.
the binding of the substrate to the polymer support does not alter its affinity to the enzyme and that the catalytic activity is not impaired by this modification.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the binding of a substrate or inhibitor to a polymer does not affect the kinetic parameters of the enzyme-catalyzed reaction.
the dextran-linked nucleoside acetates are good substrates and inhibitors and that they can easily be prepared in a one-step reaction.
dextran-linked nucleoside acetate derivatives are excellent inhibitors of adenosinase.
